posts.text:
Three loans can average 63 percent LTV and still carry 70 percent. How?

Say you hold a $600,000 loan at 75 percent LTV, a $100,000 loan at 55 percent and a $150,000 loan at 60 percent. The simple average is 63.3 percent.

Weighted average LTV multiplies each LTV by its loan balance, adds those up ($595,000), then divides by the total balance ($850,000). The answer is 70.0 percent.

The $600,000 loan is about 71 percent of your balance, so it pulls the number up. Track the weighted figure, not the simple one.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Worked example: three loans of $600,000 at 75 percent LTV, $100,000 at 55 percent and $150,000 at 60 percent have a simple average LTV of 63.3 percent but a balance-weighted average of 70.0 percent.

sources.title: Weighted Average LTV definition
sources.quote: the weighted average of all of the LTVs for such Purchased Mortgage Loans, weighted on the basis of the current Outstanding Principal Balance of such Purchased Mortgage Loans.

posts.text:
What does it mean when a lender is the loss payee on an insurance policy?

A loss payee is the party entitled to the insurance payout if a claim is made. A mortgagee clause entitles a named mortgagee, the lender, to be paid for damage or loss to the property.

Picture a $240,000 loan and a fire that causes $90,000 of damage. Because the lender is named, the insurer pays the lender for that loss, even though the policy is the borrower's. That is 37.5 percent of the balance.

Payout amounts depend on the policy.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Diagram: a $90,000 fire loss on a property with a $240,000 loan. Because the lender is named as loss payee under the mortgagee clause, the insurer pays the lender for the loss. The claim equals 37.5 percent of the balance.

sources.title: What is a mortgagee clause?
sources.quote: a clause in an insurance contract that entitles a named mortgagee to be paid for damage or loss to the property. | A loss payee is the party who is entitled to the insurance payout if a claim is made. | If your property is damaged while you (the borrower) are paying off the mortgage, the insurance company will pay your mortgage lender for this loss, even though it's covered on your insurance policy.

posts.text:
Mortgage delinquencies fell slightly in the second quarter of 2026, to 4.37 percent of loans. Look one level down.

The Mortgage Bankers Association reports that loans 90 days or more past due, or in foreclosure, reached 2.06 percent, up 49 basis points from a year earlier. Foreclosure inventory rose to 0.67 percent.

The headline rate is down 7 basis points from the prior quarter, but up 44 from a year ago.

This survey covers home mortgages, not private loans. Still, a lender can track how many loans are aging into later stages, not only how many are late.

posts.text:
The contract says $420,000. The appraisal says $385,000. What is the maximum loan at 70 percent LTV?

If the lender sizes on the lower value, it is 70 percent of $385,000, or $269,500. On the contract price it would have been $294,000. That is $24,500 less loan.

Someone has to cover that gap. The borrower can bring more cash, the seller can lower the price, or the deal can be reworked.

Which value the max LTV applies to varies by lender, so lenders can state it before the appraisal comes back.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Worked example: a $420,000 contract with a $385,000 appraisal at 70 percent LTV. Loan is $294,000 on the price or $269,500 on the appraisal, a $24,500 gap. Bars show borrower cash rising from $126,000 to $150,500.

posts.text:
Where does the property sit on the flood map?

Anyone can search an address in FEMA's Flood Map Service Center. A special flood hazard area is land with at least a one percent chance of flooding in any given year.

For FDIC-supervised institutions, a loan on a building in that area needs flood insurance for the term of the loan, at least the lesser of the loan balance or the maximum coverage available. It covers the building, not the land.

The rule names regulated lenders. Other lenders can ask counsel whether it applies to them.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Graphic titled Is the property in a flood zone. Three steps: search the address in FEMA's Flood Map Service Center, read the zone (special flood hazard area means at least a 1 percent annual chance of flooding), and check who is bound. Insurance is at least the lesser of the loan balance or maximum coverage, and covers the building, not the land.

sources.title: V-6 Flood Disaster Protection Act (Consumer Compliance Examination Manual)
sources.quote: The property securing the loan is located or will be located in an SFHA as identified by FEMA; and The community in which the property is located participates in the NFIP. (Chapter Last Updated: November 2023; regulated lending institutions must not make, increase, extend or renew a loan secured by improved real estate without coverage; amount is the lesser of the outstanding principal balance of the loan, the maximum amount available under the NFIP or the insurable value of the property.)

sources.title: 12 CFR Part 339 -- Loans in Areas Having Special Flood Hazards
sources.quote: Special flood hazard area means the land in the flood plain within a community having at least a one percent chance of flooding in any given year, as designated by the Administrator of FEMA. An FDIC-supervised institution shall not make, increase, extend, or renew any designated loan unless the building or mobile home and any personal property securing the loan is covered by flood insurance for the term of the loan. The amount of insurance must be at least equal to the lesser of the outstanding principal balance of the designated loan or the maximum limit of coverage available for the particular type of property under the Act. Flood insurance coverage under the Act is limited to the building or mobile home and any personal property that secures a loan and not the land itself.

(Document dated August 2019; refers to regulated lending institutions overseen by the FRB, FDIC, NCUA, OCC and FCA.)

Foreclosure filings hit 40,277 U.S. properties in August 2026, up 13 percent from a year ago, according to ATTOM.

Look at the stages. Foreclosure starts were 25,894, up 7 percent from a year ago. Bank repossessions, or REOs, were 5,794, up 42 percent from a year ago.

REOs are completed foreclosures, the last stage, so they can move differently from new starts. ATTOM also says overall volumes remain well below historical norms.

For lenders, a single total can hide the stage mix. Starts and REOs can be read separately when sizing exit risk.

vaultedonline.com

Stat cards show REOs up 22 percent from July and 1 in 3,569 housing units with a filing.

posts.text:
A borrower asks for three more months on a $450,000 loan, and the lender charges a 1 point extension fee. What does that do to the lender's return?

Illustrative example: at 10.5 percent interest-only, interest is $3,937.50 a month, or $11,812.50 over the extension. One point is 1 percent of the loan, or $4,500. Together that is $16,312.50, or 3.625 percent of the balance in three months. Annualized, that is 14.5 percent versus 10.5 percent.

Extension fees are negotiated and vary by lender. A 1 point fee only adds yield if the borrower keeps paying.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Bar showing $11,812.50 of interest plus a $4,500 one point fee, $16,312.50 over a three month extension on an illustrative $450,000 loan at 10.5 percent interest-only. Cards: 10.5 percent annualized without the fee, 14.5 percent with it.

posts.text:
Flip profits keep shrinking. What does that mean for a lender?

ATTOM reports that the typical gross profit on a U.S. home flip was $60,526 in the second quarter of 2026, down from $71,000 a year earlier. The typical profit margin was 21.5 percent, down from 27.6 percent.

Those figures leave out rehab costs and other expenses, which ATTOM says flipping veterans estimate typically run between 20 percent and 33 percent of after repair value.

A thinner margin leaves less room for overruns and delays. Stress test the budget and the exit plan before you fund.

posts.text:
Before funding a rehab, what can a lender check in the budget?

A lender can review it line by line:

1. Detail. Quantities and materials named, labor and materials separated.
2. Contractor quotes. One lender guide says estimates built from current contractor bids tend to hold up better in underwriting.
3. Contingency. That guide says a 5% line is commonly required, up to a 10% ceiling. On a $52,000 budget, that is $2,600 to $5,200.
4. Timeline. It can be compared with the scope and the local sales market.

Vague line items can signal weak planning or hidden costs.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Checklist graphic: four things a lender can check in a rehab budget: line-item detail, contractor quotes, a contingency line, and a timeline. Example: on an illustrative $52,000 budget, 5% contingency is $2,600 and the 10% ceiling is $5,200.

sources.title: How to Write a Fix and Flip Scope of Work
sources.quote: A contingency line of 5% (or $1,000 minimum) is commonly required on all projects, up to a 10% ceiling. Estimates built from current contractor bids tend to hold up better in underwriting. Separate labor and materials where possible. Base costs on actual contractor input.

sources.title: How Fix and Flip Lenders Determine Project Risk
sources.quote: A lender will usually review the renovation budget line by line. Lenders want a project timeline that matches the scope of work and the local sales environment. Vague descriptions can signal weak planning or hidden costs.

posts.text:
A $380,000 loan carries a 10 percent note rate. Then the borrower defaults. What does the note charge next?

A default rate is a higher rate a note can charge after a default. At 10 percent, interest-only, interest is $3,166.67. At an illustrative 18 percent default rate, it is $5,700.00. That is $2,533.33 more in one month, if the rate applies to the whole balance.

A note can instead apply it only to the amount in default. Limits vary by state, and courts may treat a very high rate as a penalty. Lenders can ask counsel to review the wording.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Comparison of one month of interest on an illustrative $380,000 loan: $3,166.67 at a 10 percent note rate versus $5,700.00 at an 18 percent default rate, a difference of $2,533.33, with a reminder that limits vary by state.

sources.title: Understanding Default Interest Rate Clauses in Contracts
sources.quote: A default interest rate clause allows lenders to charge a higher rate when a borrower defaults on payment terms. State usury laws may cap the interest that can be charged—even in default. No, enforceability varies by jurisdiction.

posts.text:
Are banks pulling back from commercial real estate lending? The latest data says no.

The Mortgage Bankers Association reports that banks and thrifts hold 38 percent of commercial and multifamily mortgage debt, about $1.9 trillion of a $5.1 trillion total, at the end of the second quarter of 2026. Their holdings grew $13.3 billion, or 0.7 percent, in the quarter. MBA also reports loans originated for depositories up 61 percent from a year earlier.

This covers commercial and multifamily loans, not one-to-four unit investor loans. Private lenders can treat banks as active competitors.

posts.text:
What is a lis pendens? It is Latin for "suit pending."

It is a notice recorded in a property's chain of title, warning that a lawsuit affecting the property is pending. One source says any interest acquired during the suit is subject to its outcome.

Picture a lender asked to fund a $210,000 loan (illustrative). A title search turns up a recorded lis pendens. Another source says it can cloud title and prevent a sale or refinancing.

Lenders can ask what the suit claims and how the title company treats the notice. Filing rules vary by state.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Three step cards: a lawsuit is filed, a lis pendens notice is recorded in the property records, and a later buyer or lender can find it in a title search. Panels note interests acquired during the suit are subject to its outcome and that rules vary by state.

posts.text:
New home construction in August 2026, per the Census Bureau and HUD:

Housing starts ran at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1,275,000, down 2.6 percent from July. Building permits were 1,394,000, down 2.7 percent. Single-family starts rose 7.6 percent to 918,000.

Two cautions. These are annualized rates, not units started in one month. And the change in total starts carries a margin of error of plus or minus 12.0 percent, so one month is a weak signal.

Lenders can watch the trend across several releases. The next one is October 20.

vaultedonline.com

Seasonally adjusted annual rates.
